assumptions: GIẢ ĐỊNH: there is no custom electrical board in the robot. The KiCad project is a DUMMY board (BOARD GIẢ, KHÔNG ĐẶT, KHÔNG ĐẶT VÀO ROBOT): 30 x 20 x 1.6 mm, two plain Ø3.2 holes H1/H2, solder pads only, no components; its schematic must match that board exactly, and native ERC/DRC must pass unweakened. It is not part of the robot frame, BOM or case. The case declares nativePCBCheckerApplies: false with its own mechanical report.

LILYGO pin facts come from Xinyuan-LilyGO/T-Display-S3 pin_config.h and schematic T_Display_S3.pdf dated 4/29/2024 (two 12-pin headers P1/P2, I2C pull-ups RIIC/RIID 10k on GPIO17/18). The header pin ORDER was not verified: wiring is by silk label ('18', '17', '3V', 'G'/'GND', '1'), and WIRING.md must tell the user to read the silk. On the touch version GPIO17/18 drive the touch IC; this design assumes the non-touch board.

GIẢ ĐỊNH: LILYGO and PCA9685 are bought with header pins already soldered (common clone PCA9685 boards ship with 6-pin input/output headers, 16 servo header rows and the V+ terminal fitted; pinout is the same as Adafruit's). If the LILYGO comes with loose headers, soldering them is the only allowed solder job and goes in CHECKLIST-RAP.md.

GIẢ ĐỊNH: the KK10-style WS2812 8-LED bar has 5V/GND/DIN pads; if it has no wires/pins, soldering a 3-pin header is the second (and last) allowed solder job. Driving DIN directly at 3.3 V from GPIO1 is assumed to work; if the LEDs flicker, the checklist fix is: lower the brightness, shorten the DIN wire, then swap to a bar sold as '5V WS2812 with 3.3V input' (no added circuit).

GIẢ ĐỊNH: LED 5V is taken from the PCA9685 output-side header V+ pin, which is the same SERVO_5V rail fed by power bank port 2 through the terminal adapter, as the brief requires. The LED is never powered from the LILYGO.

GIẢ ĐỊNH: power bank (to be bought): slim ~5000 mAh, 2 USB-A outputs, each ≥ 2.4 A, max 100 x 65 x 15 mm and 120 g, ports on a short end, and no auto-off at low current is preferred. The cradle is sized 100 x 66 x 15 plus clearance (case-owned). Its real port positions on the rear face are unmeasured, so the rear bay spans the full width.

GIẢ ĐỊNH: power wires adapter -> PCA9685 terminal are Dupont male-male, doubled (2 wires for + and 2 for -) and clamped straight in both screw terminals: no stripping, no soldering. Signal wires are Dupont female-female. Checklist: if the wires get warm, use the thicker red/black wire listed in the BOM as optional.

GIẢ ĐỊNH: the USB-A-to-USB-C cable for port 1 must carry data (for flashing) and have a right-angle USB-A plug ≤ 22 mm long; the USB-to-terminal adapter must be ≤ 22 x 20 x 15 mm. Both are BOM purchase criteria because the rear bay is 22 mm deep inside the 126 mm length.

Module sizes are generous reference envelopes, not measurements: LILYGO 64x28x12 (board about 62x26; reconcile with the LILYGO STEP), PCA9685 64x27x23 including plugged servo connectors, WS2812 bar 56x12x4, SG90 hip envelope 12.5x33x27 including tabs and gear boss (SG90 body about 22.8x12.2x22.7, tab span about 32.2, shaft about 6 mm from one end). Case and firmware reconcile with real parts at integration.

Screen window: the 1.9in 170x320 active area is estimated at about 42.6 x 22.6 mm. Its exact offset on the LILYGO board and the BOOT/RST button positions are unmeasured; the case places the lid window (target ≥ 44 x 24 mm over the active area) and a BOOT pin-access hole from the LILYGO STEP and gives a checklist test-fit. The USB-C for flashing is reached by unplugging the port-1 cable's USB-A end from the bank (rear bay) and plugging it into a PC; the LILYGO end stays connected.

Nominal body layout (case-owned target inside the sealed 126 x 75 x 47 envelope): body about 125 x 74 x 46 (x -62.5..62.5, y -37..37, z 0..46), 3 mm load-bearing walls; bank tunnel z 3..18 open at the front; electronics deck z about 18.5..21.5; electronics zone above it; lid about 2.5 mm thick with hip gear bosses passing through it. Legs, horns and knee servos sit outside the body and are excluded from the body limit.

Leg/servo geometry is case-owned: hip axes nominally at (±53.25, ±22.8), vertical, horns above the lid; each leg is 2 solid parts (upper part holding the knee SG90 pocket + lower foot) with an SG90 horn-shaped press-fit slot screwed with the SG90 bag screws (GIẢ ĐỊNH, checklist). Knee module positions are neutral-pose bounding boxes only. Left/right legs are true mirror images about the XZ plane, and front/rear about YZ; mirrored servos are handled by rotating the servo 180° (never mirroring the servo pocket wrongly). Neutral-pose STEP deviation ≤ 0.5 mm and 1°.

Part/fastener targets (case-owned, the hard limits are the brief's): 12 printed parts = base + lid + 2 shared clamp bars (front hip pair, rear hip pair) + 8 leg parts; ≤ 12 M3 screws from the owned set M3x6/8/12/20 + M3 nuts only (for example 4 for the lid and 4 for the clamp bars), plus SG90 bag screws. Electronics are held in printed pockets with zip ties and no screws; no free-standing slender posts; posts/ears ≥ 6x6 mm or Ø8, height ≤ 3x the smallest side, fillets ≥ 2 mm. Print ≤ 8 h total, ≤ 4h30 per plate, ≤ 2 plates, ≤ 220 g PETG, with the owner's profile (0.20 mm, 2 walls, 7% grid, tree supports auto). Robot mass target < 500 g including the 120 g bank (plastic target ~≤ 200 g leaves margin).

Joint range target: hip and knee ≥ ±25° without leg-leg or leg-body contact, checked by the gait simulation; report in the README if below ±20°. Firmware soft limits and offset trim range are firmware-team targets (suggested: commanded joint limit about ±35° around centre, offset trim about ±15°), not sealed values.

Servo pulse mapping (GIẢ ĐỊNH, firmware-owned target): SG90 about 500-2500 us for about 180°, centre 1500 us; increasing pulse = CCW seen from the shaft end. The default direction signs (hips +1; knees left +1 / right -1) are a placeholder until the case reports the final knee mounting at integration; the Ráp page lets the user check each joint.
SG90 plug orientation on the PCA9685: brown = GND row, red = V+ row, orange = PWM row (board silk). 2 spare SG90s are loose inventory only (BOM 'đã có'), not installed geometry.

Current: 8 SG90 can peak at about 2-3 A on SERVO_5V; nothing has been measured. If the bank cuts out during a real test, the README/checklist fix is: slower gait speed setting, then a bank with higher per-port current. No electronics are added.

Not verified (only simulated or compiled): real gait/walking, sideways crab walk, horn press-fit, print fit, LED 3.3 V data, power bank behaviour, display window alignment. These go in CHECKLIST-RAP.md and do not block 'done'. hardwareTested = false.

Deliverable ownership: board team = design/, parts.json (empty/dummy), engineering/ for the dummy board; firmware team = firmware/ (source, built binary, host tests, firmware/README.md flashing steps in Vietnamese, firmware/WIRING.md with wiring figures and wire colours); case team = case/ (CAD source, per-part STEP/STL, overview, exploded view, fastener_map.csv, mechanical report, print-check, one Print-all 3MF with named plates, TEST ONLY coupon, MATING_TEST, case/PRINTED-INVENTORY.md) plus top-level BOM.md and CHECKLIST-RAP.md. The lead writes the top-level README.md and prompts/current.md at integration from the team outputs.

coordinateFrame.axes: +X forward (front = open end of the power-bank cradle / front hip pair), +Y to the robot's left, +Z up; right-handed. Hip angles are positive counter-clockwise viewed from above (+Z). Top view = looking down -Z, front view = looking along -X from in front.
coordinateFrame.origin: ROBOT BODY FRAME: centre of the body footprint (X and Y) on the underside of the printed base (z=0 = base bottom face = bed contact face of the base). The KiCad dummy board is NOT installed in the robot; its outline/mounts below are given in its own KiCad-local frame (origin at the dummy board's outline centre, same axes/units) and have no placement in the robot frame.

firmwareBehavior: Target: LILYGO T-Display-S3 (ESP32-S3R8, 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM), non-touch, schematic 2024-04-29. Never use GPIO16 (RINT 100k pull-up), GPIO43/GPIO44 (ROM UART), GPIO3 (strapping), GPIO4 (battery ADC), GPIO21 or the LCD bus pins for anything else.

Boot: drive GPIO15 HIGH, start the ST7789 on its 8-bit i80 bus (GPIO39-42,45-48, WR8, RD9, DC7, CS6, RES5, BL38), landscape 320x170, show only Vietnamese status text, QR codes, the web address and Wi-Fi status/errors (glyphs with Vietnamese diacritics, no external font download).

Servos: PCA9685 at I2C 0x40 on SDA=GPIO18 / SCL=GPIO17, 50 Hz. Channel map CH0 HIP_FL, CH1 KNEE_FL, CH2 HIP_FR, CH3 KNEE_FR, CH4 HIP_RL, CH5 KNEE_RL, CH6 HIP_RR, CH7 KNEE_RR; CH8-15 never driven. Before the first command all channels are off (no pulse).

Power-on sequence: servos are enabled one at a time into the standing pose (neutral + saved offsets), with a pause between channels; the robot then stays still in the standing pose and never walks by itself.

Joint convention: joint angle 0 = pulse centre (1500 us) + per-joint NVS offset; hip 0 = upper leg pointing diagonally outward at 45 deg in top view, positive = CCW seen from above; knee 0 = lower leg vertical (standing), positive = foot down. A per-channel direction sign table is kept in one config file, reconciled with the case's servo mounting at integration.

Current smoothing: slew-rate limited motion, gait amplitude ramps in/out on start/stop, phase-offset gait so the 8 servos never all move hard at the same instant; target is to keep the power bank from auto-cutting out.

Gait: Kame32 oscillator gait ported to ESP32-S3 + PCA9685, non-blocking (no delay loops in the web/Wi-Fi path). 8 directions: forward, backward, left, right (sideways crab walk), forward-left, forward-right, backward-left, backward-right. If the gait simulation shows sideways walking does not work, left/right become turn-in-place and this is stated in the README.

First boot / no saved Wi-Fi: start an open soft-AP 'CuaRobot-XXXX' (XXXX from the MAC) at 192.168.4.1 with a captive-portal DNS; the screen shows QR #1 'WIFI:T:nopass;S:CuaRobot-XXXX;;' and a short Vietnamese instruction. The phone joins and the setup page opens automatically.

Setup page: lists nearby Wi-Fi networks (scan), the user picks the home network and types the password. Wrong password or connection timeout: go back to the QR #1 screen and show a plain Vietnamese error on both the screen and the page; nothing is saved.

Success: SSID/password saved in NVS (never hardcoded, never logged or echoed back to the page); the screen shows QR #2 with http://<IP>/ plus the IP address as text and 'Đã vào Wi-Fi'. Later boots join the saved Wi-Fi automatically; if it cannot connect, show a Vietnamese error and keep retrying with the setup AP available.
Holding the on-board BOOT button (GPIO0) for about 8 s after boot erases only the saved Wi-Fi (joint offsets kept), shows a Vietnamese confirmation and restarts at step 1 (QR #1).

Control page (served by the robot itself, no internet, no external libraries/CDN, sized for a phone screen, no login): 8 direction buttons + 1 light on/off button. Press and hold to walk, release to stop. The client sends keep-alive while held; the robot stops (returns to standing) if no keep-alive for about 0.5 s, on WebSocket/connection loss or a page hide.

Light: the WS2812 8-LED bar on GPIO1 (RMT), toggled by the light button, same colour on all 8 LEDs, brightness capped in firmware (target, set by the firmware team) to limit current from SERVO_5V; LEDs off at boot.

Ráp (assembly) page reached from the web UI: button to send all 8 servos to the raw centre (1500 us, offsets ignored) for fitting the horns; per-joint +/- buttons to trim each joint's centre offset; Save stores the offsets in NVS. Walking is disabled while the Ráp page is active.

Host tests (no hardware) must pass for the web pages, QR payloads, Wi-Fi state machine (AP -> STA success/fail -> erase), the hold-to-move/dead-man stop and the gait/direction math including joint limits.
Never flash, run motors or connect hardware from the pipeline; the firmware source and a built binary are delivered, flashing is by the user.

modules.interface: Lies flat, low, in the base's bank tunnel under the electronics deck; ports on its rear short face (-X); slides out the open front for charging; retained by a reusable zip tie / hook-and-loop strap; outputs PB1_5V (port 1) and SERVO_5V (port 2)
USB-A male -> 2-pin screw terminal, plugged into power bank port 2 inside the rear bay; feeds PCA9685 V+ terminal with doubled Dupont male-male wires

Right-angle USB-A plug of the data-capable USB-A-to-USB-C cable in power bank port 1 (rear bay); cable rises through a rear deck slot to the LILYGO USB-C; unplug this end from the bank and plug into a PC to flash

ESP32-S3 + 1.9in 170x320 ST7789 (non-touch), screen facing +Z under a lid window, long axis along X, USB-C at the -X end; BOOT button reachable by a pin through the case; Dupont F-F wires on header pins 18,17,3V,GND,1

I2C 0x40 servo driver lying flat on the deck, long axis along X, servo header rows facing +Z (envelope includes 8 plugged SG90 connectors and the wire bend), input 6-pin header + V+ screw terminal toward -X, output 6-pin header toward +X
8x WS2812 bar, LEDs facing +Z directly under a centred lid diffuser strip (symmetric about the body centre, not one-sided); DIN from GPIO1, 5V/GND from PCA9685 output-side header

Hip SG90, shaft axis vertical (+Z up) at nominal (53.25, 22.8), body long axis along Y with shaft at the outer end; envelope includes mounting tabs and gear boss (boss passes through lid); held by the shared front clamp bar
Hip SG90, shaft vertical at nominal (53.25, -22.8), rotated 180 deg about Z vs FL (not mirrored); shared front clamp bar
Hip SG90, shaft vertical at nominal (-53.25, 22.8); shared rear clamp bar
Hip SG90, shaft vertical at nominal (-53.25, -22.8); shared rear clamp bar
Knee SG90 in the FL upper-leg part, horizontal axis perpendicular to the leg's radial direction; nominal axis-aligned bounding envelope at neutral (case-owned leg geometry)
Knee SG90 in the FR upper-leg part; nominal bounding envelope at neutral
Knee SG90 in the RL upper-leg part; nominal bounding envelope at neutral
Knee SG90 in the RR upper-leg part; nominal bounding envelope at neutral

interfaces.name: Robot Cua A1 V4 (crab-robot-v13) — handwired web-controlled SG90 crab + KiCad dummy board

pins.pin: Input-side 6-pin header OE (left unconnected; module pull-down keeps outputs enabled)
Screw terminal + (VBUS of power bank port 2)
USB-C VBUS (from power bank port 1; also the firmware flashing port)
CH0 PWM (SG90 hip front-left, orange wire)
GPIO0 (on-board BOOT button, active low; hold 8 s = erase Wi-Fi)

powerRails.name: PB1_5V
powerRails.source: Power bank USB-A output port 1 -> data-capable USB-A(right-angle)-to-USB-C cable -> LILYGO T-Display-S3 USB-C VBUS. Powers only the LILYGO.

powerRails.name: SERVO_5V
powerRails.source: Power bank USB-A output port 2 -> USB-A-male-to-2-pin screw-terminal adapter (+) -> PCA9685 V+ screw terminal -> PCA9685 V+ servo rail (8x SG90 red) and PCA9685 side-header V+ pin -> WS2812 bar 5V. No regulator, fuse, MOSFET or protection circuit is added.

powerRails.name: 3V3
powerRails.source: LILYGO T-Display-S3 on-board 3.3 V LDO (schematic 2024-04-29: AP2112K-3.3/RT9013), taken from the LILYGO header pin silk-labelled 3V -> PCA9685 VCC (logic only).

powerRails.name: GND
powerRails.source: Common ground: power bank port 1 GND (via USB) on LILYGO, power bank port 2 GND (via adapter -) on PCA9685 terminal, joined by one Dupont wire LILYGO GND -> PCA9685 input-header GND; LED GND from PCA9685 side-header GND.

tasks.board: Build the native KiCad DUMMY board only, in design/ (+ parts.json, engineering/ notes for this board). Board: 30 x 20 x 1.6 mm rectangle, outline exactly as in the contract (board-local frame), two NPTH/PTH Ø3.2 mounting holes H1 (-10,0) and H2 (10,0), and a few bare solder pads (your choice of count/nets), NO components, no BOM lines to assemble. The schematic must describe exactly this board (pads + mounting holes), with no power bank, servo, LILYGO, PCA9685 or LED. Silk and title block: 'BOARD GIẢ — KHÔNG ĐẶT — KHÔNG ĐẶT VÀO ROBOT'. Native ERC and DRC must pass with the tile's checks unchanged (never weaken rules, exclusions or severities to pass). Do not touch firmware/, case/, BOM.md, CHECKLIST-RAP.md or README.md. Start now from this contract; nothing waits on firmware or case.
tasks.case: Design the full printed mechanics in case/ (CadQuery source) in the contract's robot body frame: body = 1 base + 1 lid within 126 x 75 x 47 (excluding legs), with in-printed pockets for the power bank (low, front slide-out, strap/zip tie), LILYGO (screen under a QR-scannable window, BOOT pin access), PCA9685 with plugged servo leads, a centred WS2812 diffuser strip, the USB terminal adapter + port-1 plug in the rear bay, cable riser slot and wire-slack space; SG90 hip pockets printed in with 2 shared clamp bars (front pair, rear pair) screwed with M3; 4 mirror-symmetric legs of 2 solid parts each with SG90 horn press-fit slots and knee servo pockets. Respect every hard limit (≤12 parts, ≤12 M3 from M3x6/8/12/20 + nuts only, labelled and reachable holes, ≤8 h, ≤4h30/plate, ≤2 plates, ≤220 g, robot <500 g), the strength rules (3 mm walls, posts/ears ≥6x6 or Ø8, h ≤3x, fillets ≥2 mm, no free-standing slender posts), ≤0.5 mm / 1° neutral-pose symmetry measured on STEP, joint range ≥ ±25° with no leg/body collision. Deliver per-part STEP/STL, overview (Đủ bộ → Bước 1..N incl. a wiring step from this contract's pins, Trước/Sau, 'Vít/tán bước này' cards, collapsed 'Chi tiết', top and front views, phone-readable), exploded view, fastener_map.csv, post/ear cross-section report, mechanical report with nativePCBCheckerApplies: false, print-check, one Print-all 3MF with named plates (long side along X, owner's PETG profile), TEST ONLY coupon and MATING_TEST files, case/PRINTED-INVENTORY.md, plus top-level BOM.md (đã có / cần mua / tùy chọn, search keywords, power-bank and cable/adapter criteria) and CHECKLIST-RAP.md. Report the final knee/hip mounting direction for the firmware sign table. Do not touch design/ or firmware/; never send a print.
tasks.firmware: Write the real firmware in firmware/ for the LILYGO T-Display-S3 (non-touch, 2024-04-29) using only the pins/nets in this contract (I2C SDA18/SCL17 to PCA9685 0x40, CH0-7 map, WS2812 DIN GPIO1, BOOT GPIO0, on-board LCD pins, GPIO15 HIGH); never GPIO16/43/44/3/4. Implement every firmwareBehavior item: QR #1 soft-AP + captive portal, Wi-Fi scan/setup page, Vietnamese errors, NVS credentials (no hardcode/no logging), QR #2 + IP, BOOT-8 s erase, phone-sized control page with 8 hold-to-move directions + light toggle, dead-man stop, sequential servo enable, slew limiting/phase-offset Kame32-port gait (non-blocking), Ráp page with raw centre + per-joint +/- trim saved in NVS, all assets embedded with no external libraries/CDN. Run a gait simulation for the 8 directions (sideways or fall back to turn-in-place, documented). Deliver a built binary, host tests that pass, firmware/README.md (Vietnamese step-by-step flashing, QR/web use) and firmware/WIRING.md (Vietnamese, figures, wire-by-wire from/to with colours, only plugging Dupont wires and tightening terminals, no measuring). Keep the direction-sign table in one config for integration. Do not flash, run motors or touch design/ or case/.
